document_metadata.title: 289、INT. RESIDENTIAL HOTEL ROOM - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Danny, betrayed by Colette under duress, accepts her apology as she's forced to leave by Quincey; trapped by fire, he plays his trumpet before the room is engulfed.

entities.name: Danny prepares to assume the identity of Tom Van Allen
entities.description: Danny dresses in his 'Tom' clothes, picks up a trumpet case, and stands before a mirror while lighting a cigarette, beginning to speak as if introducing himself as someone else.

entities.name: Quincey reveals Colette's betrayal and shoots Danny
entities.description: Quincey confronts Danny with a suppressed nine millimeter handgun, accuses him of being an informant, and shoots him in the stomach while Colette reacts in distress.

entities.name: Colette protests Quincey's decision to kill Danny
entities.description: After Quincey shoots Danny, Colette expresses shock and anger, accusing Quincey of lying about not killing Danny and attempting to go to the wounded man before being restrained.

entities.name: Quincey exposes the setup orchestrated by the Mexicali Boys
entities.description: Quincey explains that the police found nothing because they were misled, reveals that Domingo suspected Danny of being an informant, and discloses that Colette was used as a mole to confirm his suspicions.

entities.name: Danny realizes Colette betrayed him
entities.description: As Quincey reveals the truth, Danny looks at Colette in disbelief and asks if she set him up, ultimately accepting the betrayal with a bitter, ironic laugh despite his worsening condition.

entities.name: Colette justifies her actions to Danny
entities.description: Colette explains to Danny that she owed a large debt to the Mexicali Boys, that she tried to back out after falling for him, and that she was coerced into the betrayal under threat and violence.

entities.name: Cigarette falls from Danny's mouth and smolders under the bed
entities.description: After being shot, Danny's cigarette drops from his lips as he collapses, rolling under the bed where it continues to burn on the carpet, symbolizing lingering tension.

entities.name: bedroom
entities.description: An interior room where Danny prepares and is confronted by Quincey and Colette, featuring a bed, mirror, and carpet.

entities.name: under the bed
entities.description: A specific sub-location beneath the bed where the cigarette smolders on the carpet.

entities.name: Danny Flynne
entities.description: A man who attempts to assume a new identity as Tom Van Allen but is confronted and shot by Quincey after being betrayed by Colette.
entities.summary: A man on the brink of death reflects on his fractured identity, revealed as an informant posing as trumpet player Tom Van Allen, exposed during an FBI briefing, with past aliases and trauma marking his transformation.

entities.name: Colette
entities.description: A woman involved with the Mexicali Boys who betrays Danny under duress, claiming she was forced due to debt and threats.
entities.summary: A woman at a bar exchanges glances and a smile with Danny, appears uncomfortable with her boyfriend's rough kiss, is later forcibly removed by another man, and seeks help from Danny while visibly distressed in a retro coffee shop.

entities.name: Quincey
entities.description: An enforcer working with the Mexicali Boys who confronts Danny, reveals Colette's betrayal, and shoots Danny.
entities.summary: Colette is in an abusive relationship with a threatening partner who knows her family's location, endangering her and her child; Danny supports her, while an armed enforcer linked to the Mexicali Boys implicates her in a setup.

entities.name: trumpet case
entities.description: A case carried by Danny that symbolizes his assumed identity as Tom Van Allen, a trumpet player.

entities.name: cigarette
entities.description: A lit cigarette smoked by Danny that falls from his mouth when he is shot and continues to smolder under the bed.

entities.name: nine millimeter with muzzle suppressor
entities.description: A firearm held by Quincey used to shoot Danny in the stomach.

entities.name: baggie of drugs
entities.description: A bag of drugs held up by Quincey as evidence to mock Danny, implying false information was given to the police.

entities.name: Mexicali Boys
entities.description: A criminal organization that orchestrated a setup against Danny, using Colette to betray him after she incurred debt to them.
entities.summary: A criminal faction linked to Domingo targets Danny, an informant, by orchestrating a setup using Colette as bait after she incurs debt to them, posing a significant threat to Danny.

entities.name: Danny questions Colette's honesty about her betrayal
entities.description: Danny expresses doubt about whether Colette is telling the truth regarding her actions, seeking confirmation from Quincey.

entities.name: Quincey confirms Colette endured severe physical abuse without breaking
entities.description: Quincey tells Danny that Colette was brutally beaten by the Mexicali Boys but refused to give him up, demonstrating her loyalty despite the torture.

entities.name: Colette reveals she cooperated with the Mexicali Boys to save her daughter
entities.description: Colette explains that she had no choice but to betray Danny because her daughter's life was threatened, prompting emotional conflict.

entities.name: Danny forgives Colette and expresses affection before her departure
entities.description: Despite the betrayal, Danny comforts Colette, touches her face, and tells her it's okay, acknowledging her strength and beauty.

entities.name: Fire ignites under the bed and rapidly spreads across the room
entities.description: The smoldering cigarette beneath the bed catches the carpet on fire, triggering a fast-moving blaze that consumes the bedroom.

entities.name: Quincey attempts to force Colette to evacuate as flames grow
entities.description: As the fire intensifies, Quincey grabs Colette and urges her to leave, recognizing the immediate danger to their lives.

entities.name: Colette refuses to abandon Danny in the burning room
entities.description: Faced with escape, Colette resists leaving Danny behind, showing emotional attachment and reluctance to survive without him.

entities.name: Quincey threatens Colette with a gun to compel her evacuation
entities.description: When Colette refuses to leave, Quincey puts a suppressed nine millimeter to her head and forces her to choose between death and survival.

entities.name: Danny urges Colette to leave for her daughter's sake
entities.description: Recognizing the hopelessness of his situation, Danny tells Colette to go, emphasizing that her daughter needs her alive.

entities.name: Colette kisses Danny before being pulled away by Quincey
entities.description: In a final act of love and farewell, Colette kisses Danny on the lips just before Quincey forcibly removes her from the room.

entities.name: Flames block the bedroom door, sealing Danny's fate
entities.description: The fire reaches the doorway, cutting off all escape routes and trapping Danny inside the burning room.

entities.name: Danny retrieves his trumpet from the case and begins to play
entities.description: As the room burns, Danny staggers to the mirror, opens his trumpet case, takes out the instrument, and plays a few notes.

entities.name: Danny plays Saeta amidst the growing fire
entities.description: Danny begins playing the mournful Saeta on his trumpet, choosing artistic expression and defiance in the face of imminent death.

entities.summary: Danny, associated with the identity of Tom Van Allen, carefully handles and plays a gleaming horn from a case, symbolizing his identity and emotional expression, notably while facing a mirror and in his final moments as the room burns.
